correctness.rationale: The two concrete independent standard-library source files were executed. The graph is a planar 12-vertex 30-edge 20-face triangulated sphere; enumeration gives 5887 nonempty simplices. A full 23130-incidence DAG acyclicity check establishes 2866 discrete-Morse pairs with exactly one critical vertex, 109 critical three-cells, 45 critical four-cells. Signed integer gradient-path reductions supply the 109x45 attaching-degree matrix. Its rank modulo three is 44 and a specified integer 45x45 minor has exact determinant 3. This forces Smith factors 1 forty-four times and 3 once. The three-skeleton is a wedge of 109 three-spheres, so the degree matrix classifies all four-cell attachments, giving 64 three-spheres plus a Moore space M(Z/3,3). A separately enumerated simplicial boundary calculation gives mod-two Betti=64 in H3 and mod-three Betti=65 in H3,1 in H4; compatible with exactly one Z/3 torsion summand. Finite checks do not assert infinite generalization, independence, or a minimum-size example.

originality.rationale: Exact published Conjecture 11 asserts all planar matching complexes are contractible or sphere wedges. Theorem 2 only covers outerplanar graphs; the icosahedron violates the outerplanar edge bound and has integral three-torsion. Shareshian–Wachs concerns complete-graph matching and chessboard complexes, with no exact icosahedral conclusion. Engström treats claw-free independence complexes, without the graph-specific calculation. A public-research record describing the icosahedral Lovász neighborhood complex studies a different simplicial complex. Targeted same-graph, alias, torsion and wider-theorem searches revealed no decisive covering statement; bibliographic uniqueness is not proven.
residual_risks: Equivalent same-graph homotopy computations could appear in unindexed or unpublished sources.
No claim about smallest planar counterexample or minimal order is made.

value.rationale: The example disproves a named, precisely quoted conjecture in arxiv:2411.04601v2: that all planar graphs have matching complexes contractible or wedges of spheres. The finite icosahedral graph is canonical, demonstrably planar, and its integrally detected Z/3 homology excludes both types. The full wedge-of-spheres-plus-Moore decomposition identifies genuine unstable attaching-map information and supplies an exact constructive obstruction, rather than a routine numerical invariant.
